source_title: Impacts of Shunt Reactors on Transmission Line Protection
source_authors: Normann Fischer, Bin Le, Douglas Taylor, Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories
source_summary: The authors describe 70-80 percent of line shunt capacitance as a common compensation range, allowing reactors to stay connected at moderate loading. They discuss terminal sharing and switching out under heavy load. Full compensation is not universally preferable.
candidate_formula: Qreactor_total_Mvar = fraction * baseMVA * Bpu at V=1 pu; equal terminal allocation is half each. Bus BS receives negative Mvar and actual absorption varies as voltage squared.
long_line_model_source: PDF pages 2-3, printed pages 1-2, Section I: lines above 120 miles require distributed-parameter equivalent pi or smaller cascaded pi sections.
modeling_limitations: 75 percent is a declared synthetic midpoint, not an installed rating or a universal rule.
Qualifying line selection must be fixed from engineering length/charging criteria before dispatch evaluation.
A constant bus shunt follows V squared; it is not an unconstrained generator of reactive power.
Reactor energization must follow its associated line or an explicitly declared station switching policy.
Long-line distributed effects and along-route thermal current variation need separate review; compensation does not cure lumped-line approximation error.
Cable compensation and buried cable ampacity require separate engineering scope; this source does not identify installed assets.
